questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?

options.text: Pulmonary artery
Pulmonary vein
Aorta
Vena cava

questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is one of the two exceptions to the usual pattern: it is a vein, so it carries blood towards the heart, but the blood is oxygenated because it has just come from the lungs. It empties into the left atrium.

distractorRationale.a: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs
distractorRationale.c: The aorta carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body
distractorRationale.d: The vena cava brings deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium

questions.stem: The wall of the left ventricle is thicker than that of the right ventricle because the left ventricle

options.text: holds more blood than the right ventricle
must generate enough pressure to pump blood around the whole body
receives blood at a higher pressure from the left atrium
contains valves that the right ventricle lacks

questions.explanation: The right ventricle only has to push blood a short distance to the nearby lungs, where delicate capillaries would be damaged by high pressure. The left ventricle must drive blood to the brain, limbs and every organ, so it needs far more muscle to develop the necessary pressure.

distractorRationale.a: Both ventricles hold approximately the same volume of blood
distractorRationale.c: Both atria deliver blood at similarly low pressure
distractorRationale.d: Both ventricles have an inlet valve and an outlet semilunar valve

questions.stem: Blood flows from the right atrium into the right ventricle through the

options.text: bicuspid valve
tricuspid valve
semilunar valve
septum

questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve, named for its three flaps, guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle and prevents blood being forced back into the atrium when the ventricle contracts. The corresponding valve on the left side has two flaps and is the bicuspid valve.

distractorRationale.a: The bicuspid valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle
distractorRationale.c: Semilunar valves guard the exits into the aorta and pulmonary artery
distractorRationale.d: The septum is the muscular wall separating the two sides of the heart, not a valve

questions.stem: Veins possess valves along their length whereas arteries do not, because

options.text: blood in veins is deoxygenated
blood in veins is at low pressure and would otherwise flow backwards
veins are closer to the skin
veins have thicker walls than arteries

questions.explanation: Blood entering a vein has already lost most of its pressure in the capillaries, so there is little force to keep it moving, especially when it must travel upwards from the legs. Valves close if the blood begins to slip back, so it can only move towards the heart. Arterial blood is under high pressure and cannot reverse.

distractorRationale.a: Oxygen content has no bearing on the need for valves; the pulmonary vein is oxygenated and still has them
distractorRationale.c: Position relative to the skin does not determine backflow
distractorRationale.d: Vein walls are thinner than artery walls, not thicker

questions.stem: Capillary walls are only one cell thick. The main advantage of this is that it

options.text: allows blood to flow very fast
gives a short diffusion distance for the exchange of materials with the tissues
raises the blood pressure in the tissues
prevents white blood cells from leaving the blood

questions.explanation: Exchange occurs by diffusion, and the rate of diffusion falls as the distance increases. A wall of one flattened cell puts the blood almost in contact with the tissue fluid, so oxygen and glucose leave and carbon dioxide and urea enter as quickly as possible.

distractorRationale.a: Blood actually flows most slowly in capillaries, which gives more time for exchange
distractorRationale.c: Pressure falls along a capillary rather than rising
distractorRationale.d: The thin wall lets phagocytes squeeze out to reach infected tissue

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of the double circulation found in mammals compared with the single circulation of fish?

options.text: Less blood is needed in total
Blood is returned to the heart and re-pressurised after the lungs, so it reaches the body tissues quickly
Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood can mix, saving space
The heart needs only two chambers

questions.explanation: Passing through the lung capillaries costs most of the blood's pressure. Because mammalian blood returns to the heart before going to the body, it is given a second push at high pressure, delivering oxygen fast enough to sustain the high metabolic rate of a warm-blooded animal.

distractorRationale.a: Double circulation does not reduce blood volume
distractorRationale.c: The advantage is precisely that the two kinds of blood do not mix
distractorRationale.d: Double circulation requires four chambers; it is fish, with single circulation, that have two

questions.stem: Blood in which vessel would contain the highest concentration of digested food shortly after a meal?

options.text: Renal artery
Hepatic portal vein
Pulmonary artery
Vena cava

questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries blood directly from the capillaries of the ileum to the liver, so it collects the glucose and amino acids just absorbed from the gut. The liver then regulates these levels before the blood joins the general circulation.

distractorRationale.a: The renal artery branches from the aorta and its food content has already been regulated by the liver
distractorRationale.c: The pulmonary artery carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs
distractorRationale.d: The vena cava carries mixed blood from the whole body after the liver has adjusted it

questions.stem: All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, and the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back. Arteries and veins are defined by direction of flow — away from and towards the heart — not by oxygen content.

questions.stem: The pulse that can be felt at the wrist is caused by

options.text: valves in the veins opening and closing
the elastic wall of an artery stretching and recoiling as a surge of blood passes
blood flowing slowly through the capillaries
contraction of the right atrium

questions.explanation: Each contraction of the left ventricle sends a pressure wave along the arteries. The elastic and muscular artery wall stretches to accommodate the surge and then recoils, and that rhythmic expansion is felt as the pulse — which is why a pulse can be taken only over an artery.

distractorRationale.a: Vein valves move quietly and the blood in veins does not pulse
distractorRationale.c: Capillary flow is slow and steady, with no pulse
distractorRationale.d: The atria contract weakly and the wrist pulse follows ventricular contraction

questions.stem: Trace the path of a red blood cell from a capillary in the foot to a capillary in the brain, naming the chambers, valves and vessels it passes through. State one reason why this route is described as a double circulation.
markingGuide: Foot capillary to vein to inferior vena cava (1 mark)
Right atrium, then through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle (2 marks)
Pulmonary artery to the lung capillaries, where oxygen is taken up (2 marks)
Pulmonary vein to the left atrium, then through the bicuspid valve into the left ventricle (2 marks)
Aorta, then carotid artery, then brain capillary (2 marks)

Reason: the blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit — once through the pulmonary circulation and once through the systemic circulation — so it is re-pressurised after the lungs (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The route must show the cell entering the right side of the heart, travelling to the lungs, returning to the left side and only then being sent to the brain. Naming the tricuspid and bicuspid valves in the correct positions is where most marks are gained or lost, and the double circulation point rests on the blood passing through the heart twice per circuit.
